documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation Note
documents.content:
## Patient: Maria

**Date:** October 26, 2023

**HPI:** Elderly female (78yo) presenting with acute cholecystitis secondary to symptomatic cholelithiasis.  Reports abdominal pain, localized to the right upper quadrant, radiating to the right flank.  Positive Murphy’s sign upon palpation.  History reveals prior history of gallbladder issues.

**Physical Exam:** Vital signs stable. Abdomen soft, non-tender to palpation.  Assess for guarding and rebound tenderness.  Evaluate for bowel sounds.

**Management Plan:** Laparoscopic cholecystectomy performed successfully. Postoperative antibiotics initiated. Pain management with acetaminophen and ibuprofen. Monitor for complications such as biliary leak or abscess formation. Discharge instructions provided regarding dietary restrictions

diagnostics.conclusion: Right Upper Quadrant Abdominal Ultrasound abnormal findings: Acute Cholecystitis with symptomatic cholelithiasis. Key indicators: gallbladder wall thickening, cholelithiasis.
